pages.title: Jupiter moons
pages.text:
Jupiter moons
A comparison of Jupiter's four largest moons, the Galilean moons. Diameters are rounded to the nearest kilometre; orbital periods are in Earth days.
Moon | Diameter (km) | Orbital period (days) | Discovered by | Discovery year
Io | 3,643 | 1.76 | Galileo Galilei | 1610
Europa | 3,122 | 3.55 | Galileo Galilei | 1610
Ganymede | 5,262 | 7.16 | Galileo Galilei | 1610
Callisto | 4,821 | 16.69 | Galileo Galilei | 1610
Sources: Diameter values from NASA's Small Solar System Worlds Fact Sheet. Orbital periods and the shared discovery attribution/year from the German Aerospace Center (DLR), “The large moons of Jupiter (Galilean moons)”. DLR notes Galileo first observed Jupiter's moons on 7 January 1610.
